Subject: Post-call: Quantix integration recap + schema/qualification

Thanks again for your time today, Samir — good conversation and lots of alignment on the integration goals. Quick recap + proposed next steps so we have a single place to move from discovery -> POC.

High-level goals you confirmed:
- Replace current in-house reranker with embedding + reranker hybrid for most-relevant search results (50%+ precision improvement target)
- Structured responses for tool-calls (order metadata) to feed downstream workflows
- Low-latency tail (p95 <= 250ms for top queries) and predictable cost per query

Technical considerations we discussed:
- SDK setup: want an opinionated JS/Go SDK path you can drop into the search service; we'll provide a small example repo and a Dockerized integration test.
- Auth: prefer mTLS between your VPC and our dedicated endpoint for PII queries; fall back to short-lived API tokens for less sensitive traffic.
- Routing: primary route -> hosted Redwood cluster in us-west, fallback -> dedicated instance (same model, quantized) for peak spikes.
- Structured output reliability: we recommended a strict JSON Schema for the tool-calling outputs + a constrained decoding strategy (templated system prompt + sampling disabled), and a two-step validation + retry pattern (see below).

Immediate next steps (action owners):
1) Evelyn: send the sample JSON Schema and the mutual action plan (attached).
2) Quantix: share a representative query set (100 queries) and a short list of reranker metrics you care about (precision@5, dcg).
3) Dev: draft the minimal SDK example with auth modes (API key, mTLS) and a routing policy stub we can run in your staging environment.

Attachment: redwood-sample-schema.json (application/json) — contains our recommended structure for the tool-calling response (order_id, items[], total_amount, confidence, trace_id) and validation rules. Also attached: mutual_action_plan.xlsx

If that all looks right, let's aim for a follow-up technical sync next week (30–45m) with Dev and one of your infra folks. I can host.

Best,
Evelyn Hart
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
[evelyn_hart@redwood.com] | (415) 555-0182

Evelyn — thanks for the clear notes, this matches our discussion. A few clarifications from our side:

1) Data sensitivity: ~20% of queries touch PII (user identifiers). We prefer mTLS for that slice; API tokens OK for anonymized traffic. We'll need a short onboarding doc for cert exchange.

2) Reranker metrics: precision@5 and nDCG@10 are the main ones. We can produce an eval set of 200 queries and expected URIs by next Tue.

We'll plan to join the technical sync next Wed; Aisha will be our infra lead for certs.

Hey Samir / Evelyn — quick technical note ahead of the sync.

On structured-output reliability we recommend the following pragmatic pattern that balances latency and correctness:

1) Constrained decode + template: use a system prompt that constrains the token set for structural tokens (brackets, keys) and a deterministic decoding strategy (greedy or temperature=0, top_p=1) for the response body. This reduces sampling-induced schema drift.

2) JSON Schema validation: always validate the model output against a canonical JSON Schema on the client. If validation passes, accept.

3) Retry with progressive relax: if validation fails, retry server-side with a stronger constraint (e.g., explicit 'must match schema' instruction + provide a 1-shot example). Limit to 2 retries to avoid tail latency explosion.

4) Fallback routing: if retries fail or timeout, route to a low-cost reranker-only path that returns ranked items with a conservative confidence score and a note that structured output is missing. This preserves availability for the search UX.

5) Idempotency & tracing: include a stable trace_id and idempotency token per user query so retries are safe and metrics are accurate. Store the final output status (ok | schema_mismatch | fallback) in your telemetry.

Auth modes: we can include both mTLS and short-lived JWTs — our SDK will abstract that away. For mTLS we'll provide an automated cert rotation example and a small k8s Job to fetch certs into your cluster.

I'll attach a tiny example script and the sample schema (see attachment). I'll also push a prototype SDK repo to the shared Drive before the call.

Thanks,
Dev
